facts.statement: Xixianykus is classified as an alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Xixianykus is a genus of alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur

facts.statement: Fossils of Xixianykus were found in the Late Cretaceous (Coniacian-Santonian) Majiacun Formation in Henan, China.
facts.quote: unearthed in the Late Cretaceous (Coniacian-Santonian) Majiacun Formation of the Xixia Basin in Henan, China

facts.statement: The holotype fossil, designated XMDFEC V0011, was discovered in the Majiacun Formation in Henan Province, China.
facts.quote: The fossil, holotype XMDFEC V0011, was found in the Majiacun Formation in Henan Province, China

facts.statement: The species Xixianykus zhangi was described in 2010 by Xu Xing.
facts.quote: Xixianykus zhangi described in 2010 by Xu Xing

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
facts.quote: The fossil consists of a partial skeleton, without the skull

facts.statement: Xixianykus was a small animal approximately 50 cm long, 20 cm high, and weighing about 0.74 kg.
facts.quote: Xixianykus was a small animal, about 50 cm long and 20 cm high, and may have weighed just about 0.74 kg

facts.statement: Xixianykus is considered one of the smallest-known non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: It is one of the smallest-known dinosaurs (not counting avians)

facts.statement: Xixianykus exhibits many anatomical adaptations suggesting a cursorial, or running, lifestyle.
facts.quote: It appears to have many adaptations towards a cursorial (running) lifestyle

facts.statement: Xixianykus had short femurs combined with long tibias and metatarsi, along with an arctometatarsalian foot structure, indicating it was a fast runner.
facts.quote: It was about 50 centimetres long but had 20 cm legs and a short femur combined with a long tibia and metatarsus, as well as including an arctometatarsalian pes, a highly modified structure in the feet of theropod dinosaurs used to enhance cursorial capability

facts.statement: Xixianykus likely had feathers, small robust arms with large claws, and a tubular snout adapted for feeding on colonial insects.
facts.quote: It was probably covered in feathers and had small, robust arms with one large claw for each hand, as well as a tubular snout used to feed likely on colonial insects

facts.statement: Osteohistological analyses confirm that the Xixianykus remains belong to an adult individual, refuting claims that it was a juvenile.
facts.quote: Despite claims by Gregory S. Paul that the remains assigned to Xixianykus belong to a juvenile individual, osteohistological analyses show that the remains assigned to Xixianykus belong to an adult individual

facts.statement: Xixianykus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 87 to 85 million years ago, in the Coniacian and Santonian stages.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período geológico Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 87 y 85 millones de años durante el Coniaciense y Santoniense

facts.statement: Xixianykus is one of the oldest derived alvarezsauroids, belonging to the subfamily Parvicursorinae.
facts.quote: Es uno de los más antiguos de los más derivados alvarezsauroides, los parvicursorinos

facts.statement: The species name zhangi honors Zhang Xinglao.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es en honor a Zhang Xinglao

facts.statement: The time range for Xixianykus is estimated from 89.8 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.quote: El nombre del género se refiere al condado de Xixia y a la palabra griega para garra, " onyx "
